name: Cloudera, Inc. (including Hortonworks)
subcategory: Hadoop / big-data platform; hybrid data cloud
origin_detail: Founded in 2008 by Christophe Bisciglia (Google), Amr Awadallah (Yahoo), Jeff Hammerbacher (Facebook) and Mike Olson; Hadoop co-creator Doug Cutting joined in 2009. Rival Hortonworks was spun out of Yahoo's Hadoop team in 2011 with Benchmark backing and sold a fully open-source distribution. The two merged in January 2019.
openness_notes: Cloudera's CDH bundled Apache-licensed ASF projects with proprietary management software (open core, 2), while Hortonworks was fully open source (3). After the merger Cloudera pledged in 2019 to release all its software under open-source licences, but moved binaries behind a subscription. Current level 3 reflects that pledge; status under private-equity ownership since 2021 is unverified.

license_history.license: All components to be open source; binaries subscription-only

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Opening of code paired with restricted binary access; followed the Hortonworks merger (unverified)

robustness: The core technologies are ASF-governed (Hadoop, Hive, Spark and others), so the code survives independent of the company; the company is PE-owned.

key_takeaway: Draft only. Cloudera and Hortonworks are the open-core vs fully-open natural experiment of the Hadoop era: both went public, neither thrived alone once public clouds absorbed the market, they merged, the merged company opened its code but restricted binaries, and private equity took it private. The ASF projects outlived both companies' independence.
